newsitem.title: FINLAND: ERM link opens upside for Helsinki stocks - analysts.
newsitem.headline: ERM link opens upside for Helsinki stocks - analysts.

text.p: Helsinki stocks have bullish long-term prospects with the markka in Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism and valuations should improve -- as long as confidence in a single European currency holds, analysts said on Monday.
"If confidence in the Euro remains strong -- which is the scenario we currently believe -- I see this as a positive thing," said Elina Timonen, chief analyst at Merita Bank.

Analysts saw scope for Finnish valuations sector-by-sector to tend to converge over time with other European markets. But even in an upbeat economic scenario they said Helsinki would generally retain a discount to other European markets.

Nerves about the competitiveness of Finnish forestry companies -- potentially exposed to competitive devaluation by Sweden if the economic situation worsened -- dented their shares in early Monday dealings, but analysts were quite calm.
"I actually believe that even though it seems pessimistic now, there is more will in Sweden (to join EMU and link the crown to the ERM) than is shown," said Timonen.

Analysts also said that even if Sweden maintained the technical ability to devalue, such a move would almost certainly put it so badly out of kilter in the single currency project it would not be allowed to happen.
One clear trading opportunity would be in tracking Sweden's willingness or otherwise to follow Finland with an ERM link, which would eliminate even this notional risk, analysts said.

Few were willing to specify the scope of Helsinki's potential gains but Opstock's Jaakko Niemela saw -- over a two to three year period -- scope for valuations among Finnish companies to increase by 20-30 percent.
"The spread between Finnish companies and European companies will be smaller in the future," he said. "But it will take time."

Two factors which would in any case keep Finnish stocks at a discount to Europe are the Helsinki bourse's thin liquidity and the relatively high weighting of forestries in the index -- which gives Helsinki a more cyclical flavour, analysts said.
"The Finnish market is currently at a discount to Sweden which I would expect to be reduced to a very large extent longer term," said Taina Uljas of Barclays de Zoete Wedd in London.
But Sweden has a broader base and less emphasis on cyclicals so its ratings would remain at least slightly higher, she added.

On the risk side, Timonen at Merita stressed that Finland's link to ERM in itself was far less important in determining Helsinki's direction than confidence in the Euro, which itself would be closely connected to broad economic growth.
"The worst scenario would be if the political will is there but the economics start to go wrong," she said.
If for any reason the markets' faith in the Euro started to fail, this would be bearish across Europe and Helsinki would face a particularly rough ride on the periphery, she said.
Awareness of this risk could also brake the likely rise in Helsinki valuations, she added.
Assuming confidence in the Euro did hold, Finnish companies that stood to gain would be those with a strong domestic focus -- like construction and retail companies.
If it did not, companies with a low dependence on Europe for earnings would be likely to fare better.
